title: Root subgroup detection in reduced torus-stable unipotent subgroups
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Groups are affine $F$-group schemes of finite type [def-sc-group-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and subgroups are closed subgroup schemes [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Smoothness and connectedness mean [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme]. Write $\mathbf G_a,\mathbf G_m$ for [def-sc-gm-ga]. Let $G$ be smooth and connected and $T\subseteq G$ a split maximal torus, that is, a subgroup isomorphic to $\mathbf G_m^r$ and maximal among such subgroups. Write $N_G(T)$ for the subgroup functor normalizing $T$ after every scalar extension. Put $X=\operatorname{Hom}(T,\mathbf G_m)$ and $Y=\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf G_m,T)$, paired by $\chi\circ\eta(t)=t^{\langle\chi,\eta\rangle}$. Let $D\subset X\setminus\{0\}$ be finite, nonempty and $\mathbf Z$-linearly independent. For a cocharacter $\eta$, let $U_G(\eta)$ be the subgroup functor of points $g$ for which $\eta(t)g\eta(t)^{-1}$ extends to $t=0$ with value $1$, and let $Z_G(\eta)$ be the subgroup functor centralizing $\eta(\mathbf G_m)$ after every scalar extension. Let $U,V\subseteq G$ be smooth connected unipotent subgroups normalized by $T$, where unipotent means that geometric points are unipotent matrices in a faithful representation. Suppose multiplication $V\times T\times U\to G$ is an open immersion, $Z_G(\lambda)=T$, $U_G(\lambda)=U$ and $U_G(-\lambda)=V$ for some $\lambda\in Y$ with $\langle\alpha,\lambda\rangle=n>0$ for all $\alpha\in D$. For each $\alpha$ suppose given $T$-normalized subgroups $U_\alpha\subset U$ and $V_\alpha\subset V$, with isomorphisms from $\mathbf G_a$ on which conjugation by $T$ scales the parameter by $\alpha$ and $-\alpha$, respectively. Suppose these subgroups generate $U$ and $V$ as closed subgroups. For each $\alpha$ let $n_\alpha\in N_G(T)(F)$ conjugate $U_\alpha$ onto $V_\alpha$ and act on $X$ by $s_\alpha(x)=x-\langle x,c_\alpha\rangle\alpha$, where $c_\alpha\in Y$ and $\langle\alpha,c_\alpha\rangle=2$. Assume that whenever $\eta\in Y$ has $\langle\beta,\eta\rangle\ge0$ for all $\beta\in D$, conjugation by $\eta$ extends to an action of the multiplicative monoid $\mathbf A^1$ on $U$. For each $\alpha$ choose $\eta_\alpha\in Y$ with $\langle\alpha,\eta_\alpha\rangle=0$ and $\langle\beta,\eta_\alpha\rangle=m_\alpha>0$ for every $\beta\ne\alpha$. Suppose evaluation at zero is a homomorphism $p_\alpha:U\to U_\alpha$ restricting to the identity on $U_\alpha$, with smooth connected kernel $K_\alpha$, $U=U_\alpha\ltimes K_\alpha$, $C_U(\eta_\alpha)=U_\alpha$, and $n_\alpha K_\alpha n_\alpha^{-1}=K_\alpha$. Assume in addition that a word $\dot w_0$ in the $n_\alpha^{\pm1}$ conjugates $U$ onto $V$. Every nontrivial reduced closed subgroup $A\subseteq U$ normalized by $T$ contains a conjugate $\dot w U_\alpha\dot w^{-1}$ for some $\alpha\in D$ and some word $\dot w$ in the $n_\beta^{\pm1}$. Reduced means that the coordinate ring has no nonzero nilpotents; normalization is scheme-theoretic. The assertion is restricted to reduced $A$, not arbitrary infinitesimal subgroups.

proof.text: The open immersion $V\times T\times U\to G$ is injective on points over every $F$-algebra. If $z\in(U\cap V)(R)$, the triples $(z,1,1)$ and $(1,1,z)$ have the same product, so equality of triples gives $z=1$. Thus $U\cap V=1$ as subgroup functors. Also a reduced closed subgroup $B$ of $G$ with $B(F)=\{1\}$ must be trivial: for each $f\in F[B]$, the function $f-f(1)$ vanishes at every $F$-point, hence is zero by the cited vanishing principle. Evaluation at $1$ therefore identifies $F[B]$ with $F$. In particular the given nontrivial reduced $A$ has a nonidentity $F$-point.

proof.text: Consider a conjugate $B=gAg^{-1}\subseteq U$, where $g$ is a word in the $n_\beta^{\pm1}$. It remains reduced, affine and of finite type, and is normalized by $T$: for $t\in T$ the conjugation formula uses $g^{-1}tg\in T$. For $b\in B(F)$ and $\alpha\in D$, the assumed monoid action gives a morphism $c_b:\mathbf A^1\to U$ with $c_b(t)=\eta_\alpha(t)b\eta_\alpha(t)^{-1}$ for $t\ne0$ and $c_b(0)=p_\alpha(b)$. For any function $h$ in the defining ideal of $B$ in $F[U]$, $h\circ c_b\in F[t]$ vanishes for every $t\in F^\times$, since $B$ is $T$-normalized. The algebraically closed field $F$ is infinite (if it were finite, $\prod_{a\in F}(X-a)-1$ would have no root). A nonzero polynomial has only finitely many roots, so $h\circ c_b=0$. Evaluation at zero shows $p_\alpha(b)\in B(F)$.

proof.text: Otherwise, for the chosen $\alpha$ we have $p_\alpha(b)=1$ for all $b\in B(F)$. Every function in the ideal defining $K_\alpha=\ker(p_\alpha)$ in $U$ restricts to zero at every $F$-point of $B$. The cited vanishing principle on the reduced finitely generated algebra $F[B]$ says that each such restriction is zero. Hence the closed immersion $B\to U$ factors through $K_\alpha$, including its full scheme structure. Since $n_\alpha K_\alpha n_\alpha^{-1}=K_\alpha$, conjugation by either $n_\alpha$ or $n_\alpha^{-1}$ then puts $B$ back inside $K_\alpha\subseteq U$. This uses no reducedness of an intersection or of a kernel: only reducedness of $B$.

proof.text: Write the given longest word as $\dot w_0=q_\ell\cdots q_1$, where $q_j=n_{\alpha_j}^{\epsilon_j}$ and $\epsilon_j\in\{1,-1\}$. Set $g_0=1$ and $g_j=q_j\cdots q_1$. Inductively, unless Step 3 has already produced the desired subgroup, $B_{j-1}=g_{j-1}Ag_{j-1}^{-1}$ is contained in $U$. Apply Step 2 with $\alpha_j$. If some $b\in B_{j-1}(F)$ has nonidentity projection, Step 3 finishes. If none does, Step 4 gives $B_j\subseteq U$, proving the induction step. If all $\ell$ stages fail, then $B_\ell=\dot w_0A\dot w_0^{-1}\subseteq U$, while $A\subseteq U$ and $\dot w_0U\dot w_0^{-1}=V$ also give $B_\ell\subseteq V$. Step 1 forces $B_\ell=1$, contradicting nontriviality of $A$ under conjugation. This also handles $\ell=0$: the longest-conjugation hypothesis would give $U=V$, hence $A=1$. Therefore one stage succeeds, and the inverse of its prefix is a word of the allowed form.
